# emphasis-style

- ID: `MD049`
- Category: Emphasis
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: yes
- Tags: `emphasis`

All italic text uses one marker, \*text\* or \_text\_, except \* inside a word.

## Why

One italic marker throughout makes the source easier to read. Underscores do not
mark emphasis inside a word, so \* stays allowed there.

## Options

Set them under `rules.emphasis-style.options`.

- `style` (`string`, default `consistent`): Marker of emphasis to require.
  consistent takes the marker of the first emphasis. Values: `consistent`,
  `asterisk`, `underscore`.

## Fix

The fix swaps the markers. gomdlint reports italic text without a fix when the
new marker could pair with characters around it, as in \*snake\_case\*. It does
the same inside square brackets that are, or could become, the label of a
reference link. gomdlint may report a finding without a fix when the fix would
change a line with one character in brackets, such as \[x\] or \[1\], or the
lines around it up to a blank line, because it could add or remove a task list
checkbox.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

Fixes are *safe* by default and _never_ change code blocks.
```

gomdlint reports:

```text
3:33 Emphasis style "underscore" does not match expected "asterisk"
3:39 Emphasis style "underscore" does not match expected "asterisk"
```

The fix changes it to:

```markdown
# Guide

Fixes are *safe* by default and *never* change code blocks.
```

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  emphasis-style:
    options:
      style: consistent
```

Under `rules`, `emphasis-style: false` turns the rule off and
`emphasis-style: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable emphasis-style` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line emphasis-style -->
```
